content: PROJECT GLASSWING LAUNCHED — April 7, 2026. Anthropic publicly released Claude Mythos Preview through Project Glasswing, a defensive cybersecurity initiative. 12 launch partners: AWS, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorganChase, Linux Foundation, Microsoft, Nvidia, Palo Alto Networks. 40+ additional organizations granted access. Mythos identified thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities across every major OS and browser. Anthropic will NOT make Mythos generally available due to cybersecurity capabilities. $100M in usage credits committed, $4M donated to open-source security. Anthropic stated they will develop safeguards on an upcoming Claude Opus model first before applying them to Mythos. Anthropic Frontier Red Team Cyber Lead Newton Cheng confirmed the gated release. Logan Graham (frontier development lead): If we are crossing the Rubicon where you can automate these capabilities cheaply, we are in an entirely new world. RELEVANCE TO COMPASS WORK: Mythos validates the thesis that frontier models need governance beyond RLHF — Anthropic chose gated access over public release because constraint-based safety is insufficient for this capability level. Whether the compass architecture specifically is relevant to Mythos-scale governance is an open question, not a confirmed claim. The compass has been validated at 9B-26B scale. Mythos operates at a different magnitude. The architectural principle (epistemic routing before generation) may transfer. The specific implementation has not been tested at frontier scale.
